research_rationale: EO 12105 (43 FR 59465; signed 1978-12-19, printed in the Federal Register of 1978-12-21) delegates to the Civil Service Commission, in consultation with the Attorney General, the Secretary of Defense and the Mayor of the District of Columbia, authority to promulgate regulations implementing section 459 of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 659) for legal process against federal and D.C. employees' pay to enforce child-support and alimony obligations; it prescribes three required features of those regulations; it revokes EO 11881; and it preserves regulations issued under EO 11881 until the Commission modifies, supersedes or revokes them. Identity: the held Federal Register text of 43 FR 59465 (PDF page 13) prints 'Executive Order 12105', 'December 19, 1978' and the title 'Garnishment of Moneys Payable to Employees of Executive Agencies and the District of Columbia' (FR Doc. 78-35716). The seven machine clauses are the complete operative inventory: the delegation (printed with the label 1-161, an OCR misreading of 1-101), the lead of section 1-102 and its subsections (a), (b) and (c), the revocation in section 1-201 and the savings sentence in section 1-202. The order has no effective-date, sunset or termination provision. Later events: EO 12107 (44 FR 1055, signed 1978-12-28) lists EO 12105 among the orders in which, by its section 2-101, the words Civil Service Commission are replaced by Office of Personnel Management, and its section 2-404 makes the order effective on 1979-01-01; that is an amendment of the clauses naming the Commission, not an end. The U.S. Code note, the eCFR authority line of 5 CFR part 581 and the Federal Register catalog search disclose no revocation, supersession or other amendment. The delegation and the three content requirements are operative: the Commission's functions passed to the Office of Personnel Management and the regulations they authorize are still in the Code of Federal Regulations under this authority. The revocation of EO 11881 was performed when this order issued. The savings sentence is treated as operative because no held source shows that every regulation preserved by it was later modified, superseded or revoked; that is stated as a limit of the evidence, not a finding of an end.
savings_reason: The order contains one savings sentence (section 1-202): regulations, directives or actions taken by the Civil Service Commission under EO 11881 remain in effect until modified, superseded or revoked under this order. The revocation of EO 11881 in section 1-201 does not extinguish them. The functions the order delegates to the Commission were transferred to the Office of Personnel Management by EO 12107, so the savings sentence and the delegation continue under that office. No held source shows an event ending the preserved regulations.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held texts for the order number: the only held instrument that acts on EO 12105 is EO 12107 (substitution of the Office of Personnel Management, effective 1979-01-01). No held source revokes or supersedes EO 12105 or shows an earlier end of any clause. The wording until modified, superseded or revoked in section 1-202 is a contingent end for preserved regulations, not a dated end, and no held source shows the event.
scope_check: The only partial effect is EO 12107's substitution of the Office of Personnel Management for the Commission, which changes the actor named in sections 1-101 (printed 1-161), 1-102, 1-102(c) and 1-202 and ends no clause. EO 12107 does not reach the content requirements in 1-102(a) and (b).
independent_command_check: Each clause was read separately: 1-101 (delegation), 1-102 (content requirements), 1-201 (revocation of EO 11881, performed on issuance) and 1-202 (savings). The revocation in 1-201 is a one-time command; the others are standing commands.
savings_check: Section 1-202 is the only savings provision. See the savings reason: it transfers with the delegation to the Office of Personnel Management and has no held ending event.

research_rationale: EO 12139 (44 FR 30311, signed 1979-05-23; FR Doc. 79-16621) authorizes the Attorney General to approve warrantless electronic surveillance for foreign intelligence under section 102(a)(1) of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (section 1-101), to approve applications to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court under section 102(b) (section 1-102), designates seven named senior officials to make the certifications required by section 104(a)(7) of that Act and limits the authority to officials appointed with Senate consent (section 1-103 and its subsections), and amends sections 2-202 and 2-203 of EO 12036 (sections 1-104 and 1-105). Identity: the held Federal Register text of 44 FR 30311 (PDF page 11) prints 'Executive Order 12139 of May 23, 1979' and 'Foreign Intelligence Electronic Surveillance'. The twelve machine clauses are the complete inventory; subsections (a) and (b) are merged for quotation checking. Later events: EO 13383 (signed 2005-07-15) amends section 1-103 by replacing the Director of Central Intelligence with the Director of National Intelligence in (c), replacing the Deputy Director of Central Intelligence with the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency in (g) and adding a subsection (h); EO 13475 (signed 2008-10-07) amends section 1-103 by replacing (7) with (6) where it appears (the lead), adding a subsection (i) and adding a sentence to the closing paragraph. Neither revokes any part. Context: EO 12333 section 3.6 (signed 1981-12-04) revokes EO 12036, which sections 1-104 and 1-105 amended; it acts on EO 12036, not on EO 12139, and its page check is not completed in the packet, so it is disclosed here and not cited as a source. Result at 2026-10-14: sections 1-101, 1-102 and 1-103 with its subsections continue as amended, as the current U.S. Code note prints them; sections 1-104 and 1-105 were exhausted by performance on 1979-05-23.
savings_reason: The order contains no savings or transition provision. The two sections that amended EO 12036 were one-time commands exhausted on 1979-05-23 and left no continuing command, and the held later-event searches found no residual authority carried by this order other than the continuing sections 1-101 to 1-103.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held corpus for the order number: instruments acting on EO 12139 are EO 12333 (revocation of EO 12036, an order that sections 1-104 and 1-105 amended; it acts on EO 12036, not on EO 12139), EO 13383 and EO 13475 (amendments of section 1-103). No held source revokes EO 12139 or shows an earlier end of sections 1-101 to 1-103; the order states no end.
scope_check: EO 12333 section 3.6 reaches only EO 12036 and so touches only the subject matter of sections 1-104 and 1-105 of this order. EO 13383 and EO 13475 amend only section 1-103 (lead, (c), (g), new (h) and (i), closing paragraph); sections 1-101 and 1-102 and subsections (a), (b), (d), (e) and (f) are untouched.
independent_command_check: Each of the twelve machine clauses (eleven after merging (a) and (b)) was read: 1-101 and 1-102 are independent authorizations to the Attorney General; 1-103 and its subsections designate certifying officials; 1-104 and 1-105 are one-time amendments of another order and are treated separately from them.
savings_check: No savings clause exists in the order; see the savings reason.

research_rationale: EO 12208 (45 FR 25789, signed 1980-04-15; FR Doc. 80-11908) delegates to the Secretary of State and the Attorney General the functions of consulting with the Judiciary Committees under sections 101(a)(42)(B) and 207(a), (b), (d) and (e) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, delegates to the U.S. Coordinator for Refugee Affairs the reporting and discussion functions of section 207(d)(1) and directs how the Coordinator acts and notifies the Committees, reserves to the President the determinations and refugee-number decisions under sections 101(a)(42)(B) and 207, and deems earlier actions taken under delegated functions to have been taken under the order. Identity: the held Federal Register text of 45 FR 25789-25790 (PDF pages 11-12) prints 'Consultations on the Admission of Refugees' and 'April 15, 1980'. The inventory is corrected to ten clauses (see the inventory reason). Later events: EO 12608 (52 FR 34617, signed 1987-09-09), section 15, lists EO 12208 among the orders in which the words Department of Health, Education, and Welfare and Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare are replaced by the Department and Secretary of Health and Human Services; the only such reference in EO 12208 is in section 1-102(a). EO 13286 (68 FR 10619, effective 2003-03-01 by its section 92), section 49, strikes the words that introduce 1-101(a) and replaces the Attorney General with the Secretary of Homeland Security in 1-101(a); strikes sections 1-101(b) and 1-102; and redesignates sections 1-103 and 1-104 as 1-102 and 1-103. Result at 2026-10-14: sections 1-101(b), 1-102(a) and 1-102(b) (the Coordinator's functions) ended on 2003-03-01 by EO 13286; the delegation in 1-101 and (a), the reserved functions in 1-103 and the deemed-actions sentence in 1-104 continue, amended and renumbered, as the current U.S. Code note shows. No held source revokes the order.
savings_reason: Section 1-104 (redesignated 1-103 by EO 13286) deems all prior actions under any delegated or assigned function to have been taken under the order, except to the extent inconsistent with it. It is a validation sentence that continues in the current text as printed in the U.S. Code note, so actions taken before the 2003 strike remain validated. The functions struck on 2003-03-01 (the Coordinator's) leave no held residual command.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held corpus for the order number: the instruments that act on EO 12208 are EO 12608 (department-name substitution in 1-102(a), not an end) and EO 13286 (strike of 1-101(b) and 1-102, effective 2003-03-01). No earlier revocation, supersession or own-terms end exists; the order has no sunset. EO 12608 cannot be the end of 1-102(a) because it only replaces a department name in it.
scope_check: EO 13286 section 49 acts on named sections only: it ends 1-101(b) and 1-102, amends 1-101 and 1-101(a), and renumbers 1-103 and 1-104. It does not revoke the order as a whole, so the delegation and the reserved functions survive. No held source revokes a part of the order beyond these.
independent_command_check: Each of the ten clauses was read: the three Coordinator clauses ended together on 2003-03-01; the consultation delegation, the three reserved-function clauses and the deemed-actions sentence are independent commands that the current Code note still prints.
savings_check: Only section 1-104 operates as a savings sentence. It continues as section 1-103 and has no ending event in any held source.
